title: Interim Filter and Seal Kit for the Nose Wheel Steering Actuation Manifold
abstract: Interim answer to nose wheel steering jitter on the runway, fitting a finer manifold filter and a revised seal set so that contamination stops reaching the servo spool while a permanent redesign is developed.

sections.reason: Between 2014 and 2016 operators reported one hundred and six occurrences of nose wheel steering jitter during the landing roll, concentrated on aircraft that had recently had hydraulic work on the green system. In every case that was investigated on wing, the servo spool was found with fine particulate in the metering lands. The source was traced to the manifold filter, whose rating had been chosen for the original pump standard and was too coarse for the debris generated by the later pump. A permanent redesign of the manifold was already in early study but was two years away, and the reporting rate was rising.
sections.description: A finer element replaces the existing filter D3220123507496 in the steering manifold, together with a revised seal set for the manifold cover and a new bonded washer at the return port. The accumulator D3220121572714 is retained but its charging port cap is changed because the new seal set uses a different section. The non-return valve at FIN 2820WS5 is removed, cleaned and refitted rather than replaced, and the position sensor at FIN 9WS is checked for free movement after the manifold is rebuilt. Work is done from the nose gear bay in zones 711 and 714 with the gear down and locked and the ground locks fitted. No pipework is changed and no bracketry moves.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible at 0.2 kilograms. No electrical load change. Fully interchangeable in both directions. The filter change interval shortens from 6000 to 4000 flight hours, which the maintenance planning document must reflect, and the servo flushing procedure gains a step. The modification does not remove the underlying debris generation, so it was released as an interim standard with a stated expectation that it would be superseded once the manifold redesign matured.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, no production cut-in, because the affected filter rating had already been changed on the line by the time the bulletin was issued. Embodiment is a four hour task at any line station with the aircraft on its wheels.

type_data.production_impact: No cut-in; the line had already moved to the finer element

issue.reason: The interim standard is closed as superseded and is recorded as a pre-condition of the machined manifold retrofit, with a servo flush accepted in its place.
